title: The Use of AI Agents in Small Businesses: Applications, Benefits, Challenges and an Adoption Framework
content: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) form the backbone of most economies, yet they typically operate with limited staff, tight budgets and little specialist technical capacity. Recent advances in large language models have produced AI agents: software systems that can interpret goals, plan multi-step tasks, use external tools and act with a degree of autonomy. This paper examines how AI agents can be applied in small businesses, what benefits they may offer, and what risks must be managed. Drawing on the literature on intelligent agents, technology adoption and the resource-based view of the firm, the paper develops a function-by-function analysis covering customer service, sales and marketing, finance and administration, operations, and human resources. It then proposes a five-stage adoption framework and a set of research propositions tailored to the constraints of small firms. The analysis suggests that AI agents are most valuable when applied to repetitive, text-heavy and tool-mediated tasks, when the owner-manager remains in the loop for consequential decisions, and when data protection, transparency and vendor dependence are addressed from the outset. The paper concludes with practical guidance for owner-managers and directions for empirical research.
